gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Noto Sans Georgian reads modern and tidy, with curves that stay open. Dogica sits above it, heavy and widely tracked, and the short ascender stems below let the two hold their own lanes.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-glagoliti: Chunky, commanding, and spaced out wide: that is Dogica, with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. Noto Sans Glagolitic follows in a plain sans, its round letters staying clear at small sizes, which gives the pair a loud-then-friendly rhythm.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Dogica takes the heading with heavy, widely tracked letters whose curves all finish in a clear opening. Noto Sans Gothic answers with huge, bead-like counters.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Heavy and wide-set, Dogica announces itself with lowercase that nearly reaches its capitals, leaving little doubt who leads. Noto Sans Grantha keeps the reading smooth, since no bowl closes up to snag the eye.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Commanding from the first letter, Dogica spreads its heavy lowercase wide, each curve left open at the end. And Noto Sans Gujarati brings a clean sans with generous counters, which makes the shift in weight the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-g: Blunt, loud, and wide: Dogica stamps its heavy lowercase right up near capital height. But Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi settles into a plain sans with cut-back terminals, so a longer passage keeps breathing.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Noto Sans Gurmukhi reads clean and businesslike, its terminals flaring outward and its ascenders staying low. Dogica is the loud one here, so shrinking its heading would waste that heavy, wide-tracked presence.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Wide, heavy, and a bit stubborn, Dogica pushes its lowercase almost to capital height and opens every curve at the end. Noto Sans Hanunoo, a plain sans, keeps a long read easy with its open terminals.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Loud and widely spaced, Dogica hits hard with heavy lowercase that crowds up toward its capitals and leaves every curve open. Noto Sans Hebrew, a plain sans, is the one built to carry the line.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-hk: Noto Sans HK reads clean and brisk, with large lowercase and brush ends that lift away before curves close. Dogica's weight against that lightness is the pair's strongest quality, heavy and wide up top.
